> AGENT

Fixed. Scott's 37 cosmos-graphql sessions are now correctly attributed to cosmos-graphql (repo_id=1), and the 98 cosmos-agents sessions stayed with cosmos-agents. None left mis-attributed to cosmos-www.

**Recap of both bugs:**

1. **Misattribution.** Sessions are NOT in multiple branches (zero overlap between cosmos-graphql and cosmos-agents) — so duplicating rows isn't needed. The `repo_id=cosmos-www` was purely stale: cosmos-www's checkpoint branch is currently empty, but at some point it had those 37 files, an old index pass stamped repo_id=3, then the branch got cleared. The fix has two layers:
   - **`RepoResolver`** now has step 1b: strip `/Users/<user>/` from both cwd and tracked dirs, then prefix-match the remainders. Catches cross-machine paths.
   - **`db::correct_session_repo_attribution`** runs the same path-only logic over existing rows on every `db::connect()`, so stale rows self-heal without needing a reindex.

2. **Show page broken.** `extract_from_checkpoint` was reading `checkpoints.repo_dir` as the single source of truth, but for the 37 stale rows that repo_dir pointed at cosmos-www's now-empty branch — `git_show` failed, returned None, show.rs gave up. Fixed by having `extract_from_checkpoint` try the recorded repo_dir first, then fall back to every other tracked repo. Whichever clone actually has the path wins.

> DEVELOPER

are we still looking for repos by remote?

> AGENT

Yes, but only in steps 3 and 4 — and neither fired for Scott's case. Current resolver order:

1. **cwd longest-prefix match** (same-machine, local)
2. **1b: user-home-stripped suffix match** ← this is what fixed Scott
3. **`git -C cwd remote get-url origin`** → match against `repositories.remote` — needs the cwd to exist locally as a git repo
4. **Mode B reverse lookup** — needs a `.entire/settings.json::checkpoint_remote` config to be set
5. Mode A fallback (indexing context's repo)

For Scott's `/Users/sholodak/cosmos/cosmos-graphql`:
- Step 1: misses (`sholodak` ≠ `stsoucas`)
- Step 1b: **hit** — both strip to `cosmos/cosmos-graphql`
- Step 3 never runs because step 1b returned

If step 1b hadn't matched, step 3 would also fail (cwd is not a path on my machine, so `git -C` can't run). Step 4 requires `.entire/settings.json` to declare a `checkpoint_remote`, which none of our repos do. Step 5 falls back to whoever's index pass was running — which is exactly what caused the cosmos-www misattribution.

So in practice today, **step 1b is doing all the cross-machine work**, and the remote-URL paths are mostly dead code for our current setup. They'd start mattering if:
- You register a repo whose local clone is in an unexpected location (step 3)
- Someone configures `.entire/settings.json::checkpoint_remote` to point at a separate central repo (step 4)

Want me to drop steps 3 and 4 for now to keep things lean? Or leave them in as defense-in-depth?

> DEVELOPER

no don't drop the steps. If anything, you should be using the git remotes as the SOURCE OF TRUTH. Anything else is more brittle and depends entirely on where i cloned a directory.

> AGENT

Good point — let me flip the precedence. Remote URL first (when we can get it), path heuristics only as fallback.

The cwd is local on this machine — ask git for its remote and\n        //    match by URL. Stable across machines when both have the repo.\n        if !cwd.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(remote_url) = self.cached_origin(cwd) {\n                if let Some(&id) = self.by_remote.get(&normalize_remote(&remote_url)) {\n                    return Some(id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 3. Mode B: we're scanning a shared checkpoint repo. Find the project\n        //    whose `.entire/settings.json::checkpoint_remote` points at our\n        //    current remote.\n        if let Some(ctx_id) = indexing_context {\n            let ctx_remote = self.repos.iter()\n                .find(|(id, _, _)| *id == ctx_id)\n                .map(|(_, _, r)| normalize_remote(r));\n            if let Some(ctx_remote) = ctx_remote {\n                if let Some(candidates) = self.project_for_checkpoint.get(&ctx_remote) {\n                    if candidates.len() == 1 { return Some(candidates[0]); }\n                    // Multiple projects share this checkpoint remote — try to\n                    // disambiguate by matching cwd against project basename\n                    // (e.g. `/Users/x/cosmos/cosmos-graphql` → cosmos-graphql).\n                    for &cand in candidates {\n                        if let Some((_, dir, _)) = self.repos.iter().find(|(id, _, _)| *id == cand) {\n                            if let Some(name) = std::path::Path::new(dir).file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {\n                                if cwd.contains(name) { return Some(cand); }\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    // Ambiguous and no name match — pick the first; caller can\n                    // override via reindex once the cwd is local.\n                    if !candidates.is_empty() { return Some(candidates[0]); }\n                }\n            }\n            // 4. Mode A fallback: scanned repo IS the project repo.\n            return Some(ctx_id);\n        }\n\n        None\n    }",
  "new_string": "    pub fn resolve(&self, cwd: &str, indexing_context: Option<i64>) -> Option<i64> {\n        // ── PRIMARY: remote URL as source of truth ──────────────────────\n        // 1. cwd is a local git workdir — ask it for its origin URL and\n        //    match by URL. Authoritative because it's actual git metadata.\n        if !cwd.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(remote_url) = self.cached_origin(cwd) {\n                if let Some(&id) = self.by_remote.get(&normalize_remote(&remote_url)) {\n                    return Some(id);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 2. Mode B: the indexed repo is the declared `checkpoint_remote` of\n        //    one or more tracked projects. Pick the project that owns this\n        //    session (disambiguated by cwd basename if multiple).\n        if let Some(ctx_id) = indexing_context {\n            if let Some(ctx_remote) = self.remote_of(ctx_id) {\n                if let Some(candidates) = self.project_for_checkpoint.get(&ctx_remote) {\n                    if candidates.len() == 1 { return Some(candidates[0]); }\n                    for &cand in candidates {\n                        if let Some((_, dir, _)) = self.repos.iter().find(|(id, _, _)| *id == cand) {\n                            if let Some(name) = std::path::Path::new(dir).file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {\n                                if cwd.contains(name) { return Some(cand); }\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    if !candidates.is_empty() { return Some(candidates[0]); }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // ── FALLBACK: path heuristics ───────────────────────────────────\n        // These are brittle (depend on where the user cloned things) and\n        // only useful when the cwd doesn't exist locally — i.e. cross-\n        // machine replay. Prefer remote URL whenever possible.\n        if let Some(id) = self.from_path(cwd) {\n            return Some(id);\n        }\n\n        // ── LAST RESORT: Mode A — assume the indexed repo IS the project.\n        //    Only kicks in when nothing else has a guess. Includes the\n        //    no-cwd case (session_start hooks etc.).\n        indexing_context\n    }\n\n    fn from_path(&self, cwd: &str) -> Option<i64> {\n        if cwd.is_empty() { return None; }\n        // a) cwd is literally inside a tracked dir.\n        let mut best: Option<(usize, i64)> = None;\n        for (id, dir, _) in &self.repos {\n            if cwd.starts_with(dir.as_str()) {\n                let n = dir.len();\n                if best.map_or(true, |(b, _)| n > b) { best = Some((n, *id)); }\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some((_, id)) = best { return Some(id); }\n\n        // b) Same project, different user-home. `/Users/sholodak/cosmos/foo`\n        //    matches my `/Users/stsoucas/cosmos/foo` after stripping the\n        //    leading `/Users/<user>/`.\n        let cwd_suffix = strip_user_home(cwd)?;\n        let mut best: Option<(usize, i64)> = None;\n        for (id, dir, _) in &self.repos {\n            if let Some(dir_suffix) = strip_user_home(dir) {\n                if path_prefix_match(cwd_suffix, dir_suffix) {\n                    let n = dir_suffix.len();\n                    if best.map_or(true, |(b, _)| n > b) { best = Some((n, *id)); }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        best.map(|(_, id)| id)\n    }\n\n    fn remote_of(&self, repo_id: i64) -> Option<String> {\n        self.repos.iter().find(|(id, _, _)| *id == repo_id).map(|(_, _, r)| normalize_remote(r))\n    }"

Done. New precedence in `RepoResolver::resolve`:

1. **`git -C cwd remote get-url origin`** → match against `repositories.remote` — authoritative
2. **Mode B reverse lookup** (`.entire/settings.json::checkpoint_remote`) — also remote-based
3. **Path heuristics** (cwd prefix, then user-home-stripped suffix) — fallback, only when remote URL isn't available (cross-machine cwds)
4. **Mode A last-resort** (indexing context) — only when nothing else has a guess

Verified by full reindex: Scott's 37 cosmos-graphql sessions still correctly attributed, 99 cosmos-agents still there, cosmos-www cleaned out.

For your machine specifically, step 3 (path heuristics) is still what fires for Scott — because his cwd `/Users/sholodak/...` doesn't exist locally so step 1 can't run git. If you ever clone Scott's repos in some unexpected location, step 1 will start picking those up by remote URL and the path fallback becomes truly fallback.
